findings.title: The SendGrid client used for cancellation is never authenticated
findings.body: This module configures `@sendgrid/mail` with `sgMail.setApiKey`, but the cancellation request is made through the separate `@sendgrid/client` instance. Unlike `emailReminderManager`, this file never calls `client.setApiKey(sendgridAPIKey)`. Consequently the new POST to `/v3/user/scheduled_sends` will be unauthorized, the catch block only logs the error, and the cancelled reminder remains scheduled and is still delivered.

findings.title: Rescheduling still creates unbounded pending SendGrid cancellations
findings.body: The reschedule path passes `immediateDelete: true`, causing `deleteScheduledEmailReminder` to immediately POST a SendGrid cancellation and return without deleting the reminder row or marking it `cancelled`. These old bookings are not subsequently picked up by `scheduleEmailReminders`, so every reschedule leaves a SendGrid scheduled-send cancellation pending until its original send time. This bypasses the new deferred-cancellation design and can again hit SendGrid's 100 pending-cancellation limit, after which later reminders will not be cancelled.

findings.title: Cancellation state updates are fired without being awaited
findings.body: `deleteScheduledEmailReminder` is async, but these calls are made inside `forEach` and their promises are discarded; the later `Promise.all` contains neither these updates nor the SMS deletions. The handler can therefore finish successfully before the workflow reminders have been marked cancelled (and in a serverless/request lifecycle can be stopped before that happens). A cancelled booking may then retain an unmarked scheduled reminder and the cron job will not cancel the email.
